name: Residence Permit to Live with a Partner

requirements.blocker_text: Both partners must be over 21 (exceptions for couples with children); must be married, registered partners, cohabiting, or planning one of these relationships.
The sponsoring partner must hold Swedish or Nordic citizenship, or Swedish permanent residence status.

Sponsor must show sufficient income to support both partners (SEK 6,243/month single, SEK 10,314/month couple, plus per-child amounts) or taxable assets covering 2 years, AND housing large enough to accommodate both (minimum one room plus kitchen for a childless couple). Swedish-citizen sponsors in a well-established relationship (2+ years cohabiting, or 1+ year with children) may be exempt.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate, partnership registration, or cohabitation evidence
Sponsor's proof of income and housing

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sweden). citizenship_after_months (84) reflects Swedish citizens' spouse/cohabitant naturalization track: 7 years, up from 3 years under the pre-June-2026 rules (see se_naturalisation.json) -- a very large, very recent tightening specific to this pathway, worth flagging prominently since it more than doubles the prior wait. pr_after_months (24) is not independently confirmed at tier-1 precision for this specific family route in this pass (unlike se_work_permit.json's explicit 4-year figure) -- modeled as an estimate based on the general pattern of shorter PR-eligibility windows for family-based residence versus work-based residence in comparable systems; flagged as unconfirmed rather than sourced. Family reunification rules are also set to tighten further from 1 January 2027 per Migrationsverket's own reform summary (stricter maintenance requirements, extended renewal conditions, 2-year waiting periods for certain groups) -- not yet reflected in the specific figures here since those changes postdate this research pass's effective date.
